points.description: States that the frequency of light is proportional to its energy (higher frequency = higher energy, E = hf).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if the link is only implied, e.g. mentions that higher frequency light has more energy without clearly saying so for absorption.

points.description: States that the energy levels of an electron in an atom are quantized (only certain discrete energies allowed).
Explains that to excite an electron, the light's energy/frequency must match the difference between two energy levels, so only certain frequencies are absorbed.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if says only specific frequencies/energies work because levels are discrete, but does not clearly say the energy must match the gap.

points.description: States that a minimum amount of energy (threshold, ionization energy) is needed to eject an electron from the atom.
States that energy above the minimum threshold is not restricted, because the extra energy becomes kinetic energy of the ejected electron, so any frequency above threshold can be absorbed.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if says any higher frequency works because the electron is free/no longer quantized, but does not mention kinetic energy.

rubric.notes: Award each point when its central idea is clearly present in any wording; technical terms are not needed and an implied link is accepted. Part marks go to answers on the right track but vague. Extra wrong or irrelevant remarks do not cost marks unless they contradict a central idea. Restating the question earns nothing.
